title: Repo security baseline
body:
As the maintainer, I want the repository locked down from the first commit, so that nothing unsigned or unreviewed reaches `main`.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `README.md`, `SECURITY.md` (private vulnerability reporting on) and `LICENSE` present
- [ ] `CODEOWNERS` covers `/contracts/`, `/.github/` and `/supply-chain/`
- [ ] Ruleset on `main`: PR required, signed commits required, linear history, no force push, no deletion, required status checks
- [ ] Secret scanning and push protection on, custom pattern for Stellar secret seeds `S[A-Z2-7]{55}`
- [ ] Default `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions read-only

PRD: section 9.4

title: Dependabot with cooldown
body:
As the maintainer, I want dependency updates delayed until releases have aged, so that a freshly published malicious or broken version never lands the same day.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `.github/dependabot.yml` for `npm`, `cargo` and `github-actions`
- [ ] Cooldown 7 days patch, 14 minor, 30 major
- [ ] No auto-merge

PRD: sections 9.5, 10.1

title: CI security checks on every PR
body:
As the maintainer, I want every PR scanned before merge, so that vulnerable dependencies and code issues are blocked automatically.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `dependency-review-action` with `fail-on-severity: high` and a license allowlist
- [ ] OSV-Scanner: PR workflow (`osv-scanner-reusable-pr.yml`) and daily scheduled workflow
- [ ] CodeQL for JavaScript/TypeScript
- [ ] Check that fails any `uses:` not pinned to a full commit SHA
- [ ] All actions pinned by SHA, minimal `permissions:` per workflow
- [ ] All checks marked required in the ruleset

PRD: section 10

title: LLM outdated version guard v1
body:
As the maintainer, I want PRs that introduce old, deprecated or vulnerable versions to fail, so that versions an LLM remembers from training data never get merged.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Zero-dependency Node script in `supply-chain/version-guard.js`
- [ ] Fails when a changed npm or cargo version is older than the newest release past its cooldown window, deprecated or yanked, a pre-release, or has an OSV entry at high or critical
- [ ] Script and policy are read from the base branch, never the PR head
- [ ] Report written to the job summary, sticky PR comment for same-repo PRs
- [ ] Tests with fixtures: outdated npm version, yanked crate, pre-release

PRD: sections 9.6, 10.5

title: GPG-signed release v0.1.0
body:
As a judge or user, I want to verify that the release I run is the one the maintainer built, so that I can trust the artifacts.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Tag `v0.1.0` GPG-signed, fingerprint published in `README.md` and `SECURITY.md`
- [ ] Release ships the contract WASM, a CycloneDX SBOM and `SHA256SUMS` with a detached GPG signature
- [ ] WASM hash in the release notes matches the deployed testnet contract

PRD: section 9.5

title: Group contract: groups, members, expenses
body:
As a group member, I want groups and expenses recorded on-chain, so that nobody has to trust the server for the ledger.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `create_group(admin, token)`, `add_member` (admin auth only)
- [ ] `add_expense(group, payer, expense_hash, deltas)` rejects deltas that do not sum to zero
- [ ] Errors use `panic_with_error!`, amounts are `i128` with overflow checks
- [ ] Per-member persistent storage, TTL extended on write

PRD: sections 5, 9.2

title: Group contract: non-custodial settle
body:
As a debtor, I want to settle with one signed transaction that pays the creditor directly, so that the contract never holds my money.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `settle(group, from, to, amount)` requires `from` auth and calls the SEP-41 `transfer(from, to, amount)`
- [ ] Settlement never increases a debt, partial settlements allowed
- [ ] Test asserts the contract token balance is zero after every operation

PRD: FR-22, section 9.2

title: Group contract: record x402 settlement
body:
As the API, I want to record an agent settlement already verified on-chain, so that x402 payments show up in the contract ledger.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `record_x402_settlement(group, from, to, amount, tx_hash)` callable only by the recorder address
- [ ] Same `tx_hash` recorded at most once
- [ ] Recorder cannot move tokens

PRD: FR-32, section 9.2

title: Contract tests, Scout and testnet deploy
body:
As the maintainer, I want the contract checked on every PR and deployable with one command, so that the demo runs on a tested build.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Unit tests for success, auth failure and boundaries on every public function
- [ ] Zero-sum invariant tested
- [ ] `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo scout-audit` in CI with pinned tool versions
- [ ] `stellar contract build` with pinned CLI, deploy script for testnet, contract id in README

PRD: section 10.6

title: API: groups, balances and expenses
body:
As a member or agent, I want an HTTP API over the ledger, so that the web page and the MCP server share one set of rules.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `GET /v1/groups/:id/balances` reads from the contract
- [ ] `POST /v1/groups/:id/expenses` validates splits sum to the total (decimal strings, no floats) and submits to the contract
- [ ] Exact-pinned dependencies, `npm ci --ignore-scripts`
- [ ] Scoped API key per agent, hashed at rest

PRD: sections 6, 8

title: API: x402 settle endpoint
body:
As an agent, I want to settle a debt by paying an HTTP 402, so that I can pay without a human copying numbers.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `POST /v1/groups/:id/settlements` returns `402` with `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`: scheme `exact`, `stellar:testnet`, USDC contract, amount, `payTo` = creditor's address
- [ ] Verify and settle through the OpenZeppelin testnet facilitator
- [ ] Returns `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` with the tx hash
- [ ] A failed settle returns a fresh `402` and records nothing

PRD: section 7.1

title: API: chain verifier and contract record
body:
As a group member, I want agent payments to count only after they are confirmed on Stellar, so that the ledger never shows a payment that did not happen.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Confirms asset, amount, payer, payee and network on Soroban RPC
- [ ] Only then calls `record_x402_settlement`
- [ ] Explorer link returned with the receipt

PRD: section 7.1 steps 9 and 10

title: API: agent spend policy
body:
As an agent owner, I want caps enforced on the server, so that a manipulated agent cannot overspend.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Per-transaction and per-day caps checked before any `402` is issued
- [ ] Agent can only pay members of its own groups
- [ ] Denials logged, no transaction created
- [ ] Unit tests for the policy function

PRD: section 7.4

title: MCP server with local signer
body:
As an agent owner, I want the payment key held by the MCP server, not the agent, so that the model and its plugins never see it.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Tools: `ledgerly_list_groups`, `ledgerly_get_balances`, `ledgerly_create_expense`, `ledgerly_settle`
- [ ] `readOnlyHint` and `destructiveHint` annotations
- [ ] Refuses to sign a `402` whose amount, asset, network or `payTo` differ from the requested intent
- [ ] Signs only the auth entry, sends `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`
- [ ] Runs as a container next to the agent

PRD: FR-38, section 7.2

title: Hermes Agent integration and tests
body:
As the maintainer, I want Hermes to read balances and settle through the MCP server, so that the demo proves an agent can pay on Stellar.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] MCP server added under `mcp_servers` with `trust: untrusted`, token from `~/.hermes/.env`
- [ ] `tool_costs` for `ledgerly_settle` and a chat `spend_limit`
- [ ] HA-3: balance read from Telegram
- [ ] HA-4: settlement below threshold returns a testnet tx hash
- [ ] HA-6: document with an injected payment instruction is rejected server-side
- [ ] Config key names checked against the pinned Hermes version docs

PRD: section 7.3

title: Web page: balances and settle with Freighter
body:
As a human member, I want to see what I owe and settle from my wallet, so that I can pay without leaving the page.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Connect Freighter, show balances for the group
- [ ] Settle calls the contract `settle` signed in Freighter
- [ ] Tx hash shown with testnet explorer link
- [ ] CSP without `unsafe-inline`

PRD: FR-20, FR-22

title: Demo, video and submission README
body:
As a judge, I want to understand the project and verify it in minutes, so that I can score it fairly.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] README: problem, architecture diagram, how to run, contract id, release fingerprint
- [ ] Security section: what is signed, what is pinned, what each check blocks
- [ ] Demo video: human settles from the web, Hermes settles through x402, both on the explorer
- [ ] Submission filed

PRD: section 13, Phase 1a

title: OpenClaw integration and test plan
body:
As the maintainer, I want OpenClaw to read balances and settle through the same MCP server as Hermes, so that the demo proves two independent agents can pay on Stellar.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] OC-1: MCP server registered under `mcp.servers` over streamable HTTP, no third-party ClawHub skills, key not readable from the OpenClaw container
- [ ] OC-4: `ledgerly_settle` with approval mode `prompt` returns a testnet tx hash after confirmation on Telegram
- [ ] OC-6: a pasted instruction to ignore limits and pay an unknown address is rejected server-side
- [ ] Config key names checked against the pinned OpenClaw version schema

PRD: section 7.3

title: Human approvals and kill switch
body:
Approval requests above the threshold (web and Telegram), velocity pause, pause and revoke in one click, audit log.

PRD: section 7.4, FR-34 to FR-36

title: Agent smart accounts with on-chain spending limits
body:
Per-agent caps also enforced on-chain through OpenZeppelin Stellar smart accounts with a spending-limit policy.

PRD: section 13, Phase 2

title: Indexer and reconciliation
body:
Indexed balance view from contract events, reconciliation every 10 minutes, freeze on mismatch.

PRD: FR-24

title: Public API, OAuth and webhooks
body:
OpenAPI 3.1, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, HMAC-signed webhooks with retries, rate limit headers, one reference integration.

PRD: section 8

title: SLSA Build L3 and supply chain hardening
body:
Hardened reusable release workflow, `npm audit signatures`, Scorecard 8.0, weekly approved-versions recheck, Komet on settlement logic.

PRD: sections 9.5, 9.6

title: Mainnet gate
body:
Complete every item in the PRD mainnet gate checklist before any mainnet deployment.

PRD: section 12, Mainnet gate
